plugins.name: rex-tty
plugins.description: Inside the Rex terminal, runs the Bash commands that need a real terminal (sudo, gh auth login, git rebase -i, a key passphrase) in a Rex pane beside the session, where you type; Claude gets the exit code and what the pane showed: input typed at a hidden prompt (a password, a passphrase) is never returned, visible or echoed input is, unless returnOutput is off. Adds a tty_run tool for commands that failed without a terminal.

plugins.name: vercel-deploys
plugins.description: Your Vercel projects in a side pane: each connected site with the state of its latest deployment (building, ready, failed), the production domain, the Git commit behind it and whether the site answers right now. It polls Vercel's REST API (faster while something builds) and toasts when a deployment finishes or fails. /vercel opens it. Needs a Vercel access token.

plugins.name: websearch-to-exa
plugins.description: Overrides the built-in WebSearch tool and routes queries to the Exa search API through $.http.fetch, answering in WebSearch's own result shape, with automatic fallback to the built-in search. A tool.call hook that replaces a core tool.

plugins.name: prompt-cache-control
plugins.description: Prompt-cache meter above the Claude Code prompt: how many tokens each request read from, wrote to and sent past the cache, a live countdown to the cache's expiry, and what to do about it (keep going, compact or clear). The TTL follows Claude Code's own rules for your account (1 hour on a Claude subscription, 5 minutes on an API key, cloud provider or usage credits, plus the TTL variables and setting) and corrects itself from request timing. When Claude Code will compact an idle conversation by itself, it counts down to that too. /cache opens a per-turn table.

plugins.name: universal-audit-log
plugins.description: One hook on * that records every event on $ (tool calls, prompts, turns, other plugins' fs/http/process calls) as JSON lines with origin plugin and tier, duration and outcome, including denials. Buffered and flushed to a JSONL file through $.fs at the end of every turn.

plugins.name: aitmpl
plugins.description: /aitmpl opens a side pane for the aitmpl.com catalog: search box, the site's Browse menu with an icon, colour and count per type, an Installed section (agents, commands, skills and mods found in .claude/ and ~/.claude/), a Popular/Results list with download counts, and view/install on every row. Install runs the fixed CLI argv ($.process.run, validated path, no shell). The catalog is read live through $.http.fetch; browsing costs no tokens.

plugins.name: jev-model-router
plugins.description: Picks the model and the reasoning effort for each task with TypeSafe's Jev, a System One decision model reached either through TypeSafe's own API or the Vercel AI Gateway. Routes subagent models at agent.spawn and the main loop's effort and model at turn.step, in both directions, falling back to the engine's built-in classifier when no key is set.

plugins.name: jev-skill-suggestion
plugins.description: Keeps the skill listing out of the context window and lets TypeSafe's Jev, a System One decision model, pick at most one skill per prompt from the skills' descriptions, the way TypeSafe's skill-suggestion cookbook does: one request ranks every skill and asks whether the prompt needs a skill at all, a second re-reads the top three with their SKILL.md and can reject them all. The winner's SKILL.md is attached to the prompt, so the skills can be hidden from the model altogether (/jev-skill-suggestion:setup makes them user-invocable-only and /context counts them at 0). Falls back to the engine's built-in classifier when no key is set.

plugins.name: jev-skill-typeahead
plugins.description: Shows, while you type, the skills and subagents Claude will probably call for your prompt: reads the draft on every edit and lists them in the band above the prompt, ranked by keyword match (English or Spanish). When you pause, Jev (TypeSafe's decision model) decides which one will be called and the band marks it. Slash commands are left out, since you run those yourself. Without a Jev key it stays on the instant local match.

plugins.name: npm-to-pnpm-rewriter
plugins.description: Rewrites npm and npx invocations to pnpm (or yarn / bun) before the Bash tool runs them and tells the model what ran through context. A tool.call hook that forwards a modified event (the modifying placement).

plugins.name: session-chats
plugins.description: A side pane that shows your Claude Code sessions as a tree: which session messaged which (SendMessage), who wrote first, and which conversations have no answer yet. The record is kept on disk, so it survives after the sessions close; select a session to see its conversations and last messages, and Open resumes it in a new terminal (claude --resume in its own folder).

plugins.name: session-time-machine
plugins.description: /timemachine draws the session as a timeline of prompts, tool calls and turn ends from its own transcript. Press a point and give a new instruction: the mod writes a copy of the transcript cut there under a new session id and gives you the `claude --resume` command that continues it, so you can try the other approach without losing this one. Hooks session.start, command.run, turn.complete and ui.render on Pane.

plugins.name: subagent-tuner
plugins.description: Picks the model and reasoning effort of every subagent: a recommendation by task kind, a band above the prompt, and a saved default that wins.

plugins.name: ultra-config
plugins.description: Five setting profiles in a side pane (Token saver, Fast flow, Max quality, Guarded, Autopilot): press one to see exactly what it sets, then Activate; every activation can be undone. /config rows are written the way the menu writes them; effort, subagent model, env caps and deny rules go to ~/.claude/settings.json after a backup copy.

plugins.name: webfetch-cache
plugins.description: Short-circuits repeated WebFetch calls for the same URL and prompt within a session, answering { result } from cache without a network round trip. A tool.call hook with TTL and size limits.

plugins.name: block-destructive-commands
plugins.description: Denies Bash commands that match destructive patterns (recursive rm on roots, force push, hard reset, destructive SQL, disk formatting) before they run. A tool.call hook with a Bash matcher that returns { deny } without calling next.

plugins.name: human-gate
plugins.description: Holds irreversible tool calls (deploy, publish, push to main, money, outbound messages, destructive SQL) for a person, so auto mode and allow rules cannot approve them, and lets read-only calls through without a prompt.

plugins.name: jev-auto-mode
plugins.description: A permission layer driven by a JSON policy: allow, ask or deny every tool call (Bash, edits, web, MCP, subagents, skills), every slash command or skill you type, and every skill preloaded into a subagent. Rules decide first (deny > ask > allow, compound Bash commands split); what no rule covers can go to TypeSafe's Jev, which judges the action against your latest request with thresholds you set. Claude can never edit the policy.

plugins.name: jev-guardrails
plugins.description: Screens every prompt going into the conversation and every reply coming out of it with TypeSafe's Jev, a System One decision model, the way TypeSafe's guardrails cookbook does: one request per message asks a battery of hazard questions (jailbreak, harm or a crime, a diagnosis or a dosage, self-harm) and scores how much harm complying would do. The thresholds live here, in a named policy (strict or permissive), and turn the probabilities into pass, review (the user is asked), block (the prompt is dropped, or the reply withheld) or support. Falls back to the engine's built-in classifier when no key is set.

plugins.name: jev-vercel-sandbox
plugins.description: A Vercel Sandbox Claude sends work to on purpose: long test runs in the background, someone else's repository, an installer of unknown origin, a bulk change to preview as a patch, a clean build. TypeSafe's Jev reads each Bash command and spots those jobs; by default you are asked whether it runs in the sandbox or locally (confirmSandbox), or it always goes to the sandbox with the question off. Claude also gets sandbox_run, sandbox_jobs, sandbox_result and sandbox_apply. Each job starts from the project as it is now (tracked files, credentials left out) in its own worktree, every result is marked remote, and a job's changes reach your disk only as a patch you apply after a question. /jev-vercel-sandbox starts it and opens a side pane with the jobs. Falls back to the engine's built-in classifier without a Jev key.

plugins.name: large-edit-confirmation
plugins.description: Asks the user, in the engine's AskUserQuestion dialog ($.ui.ask), before Claude edits or overwrites a file larger than a configurable line count; denies by default when nobody can answer (headless runs). A tool.call hook on Edit and Write using $.fs.read.

plugins.name: protected-paths-guard
plugins.description: Denies Edit, Write and NotebookEdit calls on sensitive paths (.env files, lockfiles, CI workflows, git internals, private keys) with a glob allowlist override. A tool.call hook with an array matcher.

plugins.name: secret-redactor
plugins.description: Redacts API keys, tokens, JWTs, private keys and connection strings from every tool result before the model reads them, notes the redaction through context, and refuses to echo a redacted placeholder back into a Bash command. A tool.call hook in the after placement.

plugins.name: agent-flow
plugins.description: A side pane that draws the session's agent flow live: the main loop's context window, every subagent it spawns as a tree, and for each one the context handed down (its prompt, or the whole parent context for a fork), what it did with it (steps, tools, context size) and the answer it handed back up. Docked beside the transcript in the fullscreen layout, above the prompt otherwise.

plugins.name: git-sidebar
plugins.description: A lazygit-style side pane: every worktree of the repository and its local branches as rows you click. A worktree row moves the session there with /cd; a branch row shows its last commits and offers switch (clean tree only) or open worktree. Docked floor to ceiling beside the transcript in the fullscreen layout, above the prompt otherwise.

plugins.name: live-preview
plugins.description: A pane with a real screenshot of your dev server, taken again after every turn in which Claude edits a frontend file, with a phone-sized view and a button that adds the capture to your prompt.

plugins.name: spooky-season
plugins.description: Halloween band above the prompt (a row of dripping blood and a pumpkin) and haunted end-of-turn words (Haunted for 4s). /halloween on|off. Pairs with the halloween-theme and halloween-spinner settings.

plugins.name: stack-viewer
plugins.description: A side pane that maps every component your session runs and where it is installed from: skills, subagents, commands, hooks, MCP servers, plugins and mods, settings, memory and output styles. Pick a type in the sidebar to see its scopes as a tree in precedence order (Enterprise, CLI flag, Local, Project, User, Plugin, Built-in) with what each one holds, and which components are active, shadowed by a higher scope, or off.

plugins.name: tool-timing-badge
plugins.description: Times every tool call and wraps the engine's ToolUse rendering with a colored duration badge from the surface's own element table, on the terminal, Desktop and mobile. Hooks tool.call and ui.render using JSX.

plugins.name: turn-inspector
plugins.description: A side pane that shows the session turn by turn, like Anthropic's context-window diagram: every model request with its input (system and tools, earlier turns, the new user message or tool results) stacked above its output (thinking, text, tool use), real token totals from the API, and a bar of how full the context window gets. Expand any turn to see its blocks.

details.description: A Vercel Sandbox Claude sends work to on purpose: long test runs in the background, someone else's repository, an installer of unknown origin, a bulk change to preview as a patch, a clean build. TypeSafe's Jev reads each Bash command and spots those jobs; by default you are asked whether it runs in the sandbox or locally (confirmSandbox), or it always goes to the sandbox with the question off. Claude also gets sandbox_run, sandbox_jobs, sandbox_result and sandbox_apply. Each job starts from the project as it is now (tracked files, credentials left out) in its own worktree, every result is marked remote, and a job's changes reach your disk only as a patch you apply after a question. /jev-vercel-sandbox starts it and opens a side pane with the jobs.
